string-array.name: tips_samsung
string-array.item: Device care > Battery > Background usage limits: add BabyLock to “Never sleeping apps”.
For Fortress Mode: Security and privacy > More security settings > Pin app, with “Ask for PIN before unpinning”.

string-array.name: tips_xiaomi
string-array.item: Settings > Apps > BabyLock > Battery saver: “No restrictions”.
On the same screen, turn on “Autostart”.
Other permissions: allow “Display pop-up windows while running in the background”.
In Recents, hold BabyLock and tap the lock so it isn\'t closed.
If the notification shade still comes down: in Settings, search for “App pinning” and turn it on. See the steps in “Does the notification shade still open?”.

string-array.name: tips_oppo
string-array.item: Settings > Battery: allow background activity for BabyLock.
Turn on auto launch and lock the app in Recents.

resources.string: Does the notification shade still open?
The notification shade opened during the lock
On some phones (like Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO) the system lets the shade come down even with BabyLock. It gets no touches and BabyLock tries to close it, but you can block it for good:

string-array.name: shade_pin_steps
string-array.item: Open Settings and search for “Pin” (the name varies: “App pinning”, “Screen pinning” or “Pin app”).
Turn it on, and also “Ask for PIN before unpinning” if you see it.
Open the video, tap the recent apps button, tap the app icon and choose “Pin”.
Then lock BabyLock as usual. With the app pinned, the notification shade won\'t come down.
